name: Scent layering (body wash, lotion, fragrance)

lead: Scent layering uses products from the same scent family, such as body wash, lotion and fragrance, so the smell builds, lasts longer and feels coherent.

The fragrance industry promotes a version of it: scented bath oil, shower gel or lotion in the morning, a lighter eau de toilette in the afternoon, and perfume at pulse points in the evening. General references say hydrated skin holds fragrance longer. No published trials of layering were found.

paras: People pick matching or complementary products, apply wash and lotion after showering, then add fragrance on top, and refresh through the day.
Fragrance ingredients can be allergenic, and more scented products means more potential exposure. No layering-specific studies were found.

angle.text: Users stack matching body wash, lotion and fragrance so their scent builds in layers and lasts longer through the day. The fragrance industry promotes versions of the practice.

lead: Scent layering is the practice of using matching or complementary scented products, such as body wash, lotion and fragrance, in sequence so the smell builds and lasts longer. The fragrance industry promotes a version of it: scented bath oil, shower gel or lotion in the morning, a lighter eau de toilette in the afternoon, and perfume at pulse points in the evening.[1]
No published trials of layering were found. General references say hydrated skin holds fragrance longer and that diet, medications and dry skin can alter how a scent develops.[1]

paras: Typical longevity is described as about 2 hours for cologne, 2 to 4 for eau de toilette and up to 6 to 8 for perfume, and concentration labels are imprecise between brands.[1] Layering within one scent family is described by proponents as a way to extend these times.

Natural and synthetic perfume materials can include allergenic compounds, and a long history of use does not by itself establish safety.[1] Stacking several scented products increases the number of fragrance ingredients in contact with skin.

lore.intro: Layering is discussed as a way to make a scent last and read as intentional.

claims.claim: Matching body wash, lotion and fragrance makes scent last longer
